title: Nearline queryable feature-store for Console analytics
creator: Avery Kim
description: Create a nearline, queryable feature-store layer in the warehouse to serve Console use cases that require low-latency access to precomputed entity features (tenant, route, session, model-variant) for dashboards, heatmaps, and SLA attribution. This layer bridges streaming events (ingest) and downstream denormalized marts by providing compact, time-windowed feature rows optimized for selective ad-hoc queries.
background_and_problem: Current console analytics pipelines produce heavy, wide denormalized marts that are expensive to scan for ad-hoc per-tenant queries (for troubleshooting, product analytics, and cost-attribution). Teams repeatedly rebuild the same aggregates at query-time. We need a compact, materialized feature layer that: 1) supports sub-second single-tenant/route lookups, 2) retains short-horizon temporal features (last 24h/7d), and 3) is writable from streaming ETL with incremental CDC-friendly updates.
goals: 1) Design a row-oriented feature table schema for tenant+route+time_bucket features with TTL semantics. 2) Implement streaming writes (beam/kafka->nearline transformer->warehouse). 3) Expose dbt models and Snowflake materialized views for console dashboards and notebook exploration. 4) Add automated data quality checks and cost guardrails.
non_goals: Not attempting to replace long-term historical marts or full sessionization. This ticket does not include UI work; it only provides the backend feature layer and example queries for Console product owners.
proposed_schema:
Feature table name: analytics.nearline_features_v1
Primary key: (tenant_id, route_id, feature_ts)
Columns (examples): tenant_id STRING, route_id STRING, feature_ts TIMESTAMP, last_invocation_ts TIMESTAMP, invocation_count_1h INT, avg_latency_1h FLOAT, hot_path_flag BOOLEAN, top_model_variant STRING, kv_cache_hit_rate_1h FLOAT, token_cost_24h FLOAT, source_partition STRING
Storage/partitioning: partition by feature_date (date_trunc('day', feature_ts)), cluster by tenant_id, route_id. TTL: retain 30 days with micro-partition compaction daily.
write_path_and_ingest: Streaming sources: Kafka topics (route-invocations, model-signals). Transform: small stateless transformer service performs upserts (merge-on-write) using micro-batches (~1 minute). Use warehouse COPY/streaming ingest or Snowpipe for nearline delivery. Offline fallback: batch job hourly to backfill gaps.
dbt_and_transformations: Implement dbt models in analytics/nearline/ models: nearline_features_v1_raw -> nearline_features_v1_staging -> nearline_features_v1. Use incremental dbt with unique_key (tenant_id, route_id, feature_ts). Add tests: not_null on tenant_id/feature_ts, freshness on last_update < 2m, accepted_range checks for numeric fields.
query_examples:
-- single tenant recent features
SELECT * FROM analytics.nearline_features_v1 WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant_123' AND feature_ts >= dateadd(hour, -6, current_timestamp()) ORDER BY feature_ts DESC LIMIT 500;

-- heatmap aggregation by route
SELECT route_id, count(*) as invocations, avg(avg_latency_1h) as avg_lat FROM analytics.nearline_features_v1 WHERE feature_ts >= dateadd(day, -1, current_timestamp()) GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY invocations DESC LIMIT 100;
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): schema and streaming transformer POC for a single tenant, dbt models and tests. Phase 2 (2 weeks): scale streaming writes to 10% traffic, add compaction and TTL policies, add monitoring dashboards. Phase 3 (1 week): onboard Console dashboards and export example queries; run parallel validation against existing marts; flip traffic after 2 days of validation.
metrics_and_success_criteria: 1) Median single-tenant query latency for recent features < 200ms. 2) 30% reduction in bytes scanned for typical per-tenant console queries. 3) Accuracy parity with existing hourly mart aggregates for >99% sampled checks. 4) No regression in daily ETL cost >5%.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: high ingest throughput could cause frequent micro-partitions leading to storage overhead. Mitigation: enforce micro-batch window of 60s, daily compaction job.
Risk: schema churn for feature set. Mitigation: versioned table (nearline_features_v1 -> v2) and dbt schema tests.
Risk: tenant spikes causing hot partitions. Mitigation: cluster keys and read replica promotion for heavy tenants.
security_and_compliance: Feature table contains tenant identifiers and aggregated telemetry only. No PII. Access controlled via warehouse role analytics_nearline_reader and audit logging enabled. If customer requires additional controls, follow Private deployment RBAC pattern.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Streaming pipeline writes successful POC for at least one production tenant with observed end-to-end latency < 90s. 2) dbt incremental build passes all tests in CI and produces nearline_features_v1. 3) Example Console dashboard queries return expected results and meet latency targets. 4) Data quality monitoring alerts when freshness > 5 minutes.
owner_next_steps: Diego: spin up Snowflake dev schema, create initial DDL and dbt model. Avery: implement transformer POC and the ingest consumer. Schedule sync with Console PM for example queries and validation. Add monitoring dashboard items to observability board.
